reasons: Several checks read files that git does not track, so they can fail on a clean copy until a replay is run.
Checks match exact phrases in SPEC.md, so editorial changes can break them.
Not run in this review, so the current pass or fail state is unknown.

terms.meaning: the test runner that finds and runs the checks in this file
a place where the written specification and the built software differ
the list of known divergences kept at the end of SPEC.md

used_by: Not visible in the files shown. Runs as part of the pytest suite.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Sets up the register rules and entry table
sections.what: Holds the file's explanation, the pattern for reading entries out of SPEC.md, the path to the spec, and the table of every divergence id with its status (amended, deferred, or both).
sections.why: The table is the record that a person has read each entry. A new entry in the spec fails the check until its id is added here.
sections.watch_out: Adding an id here without reading its entry defeats the check, and the status must match what the spec text says.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Lists covered sections and the unmeasured agreement terms
sections.what: Lists every spec section the register must account for. It also holds two word sets used for the confidence measure: one naming the features of a score when agreement was not measured, and one naming the features that would falsely claim it was.
sections.why: Likely reason: the confidence field is required with no default, so each hand-built test block must name the features that produced its score.
sections.watch_out: If a section is renamed in SPEC.md, its entry here fails the check until it is updated.

sections.name: register
sections.title: Reads the register from the spec
sections.what: Returns the part of SPEC.md from the register heading to the end of the file.
sections.why: Other checks read only the register, so they cannot pass on text elsewhere in the spec.
sections.watch_out: It depends on the exact register heading text, so a renamed heading breaks every check that uses it.

sections.name: entries
sections.title: Pulls each register entry out by id
sections.what: Finds every entry in the register and returns a lookup by id, with its status, date and subject.
sections.why: Lets the checks compare the spec's entries with the REGISTERED table.
sections.watch_out: An entry heading written in a different shape is silently skipped, so it is never checked.

sections.name: entry_body
sections.title: Returns the text of one entry
sections.what: Returns the text of a single named entry, stopping at the next entry.
sections.why: A check about one entry cannot pass on the wording of a neighbouring entry.
sections.watch_out: Relies on each entry heading using the same pattern, so an odd heading returns the wrong or empty text.

sections.name: section
sections.title: Returns one section of the spec
sections.what: Returns the text of one named section of SPEC.md between two heading markers.
sections.why: A check about one section cannot pass on text from a different section.
sections.watch_out: If the end marker is missing, the text runs to the end of the file and a check could match later text.

sections.name: TestTheRegisterIsComplete
sections.title: Checks the register matches the table
sections.what: Checks the register and the table in this file list the same ids with the same statuses, every covered section is mentioned, and the register is the last section of the spec.
sections.why: The docstring says a new divergence must fail here until someone reads it, because a silent register is the failure this file exists to catch.
sections.watch_out: A section added after the register would not be parsed, and the entries would go quiet; the last-section check guards against this.

sections.name: registered_commentary
sections.title: Reads the commentary above the table
sections.what: Reads the explanatory paragraph above the REGISTERED table directly from this file's source.
sections.why: The docstring explains that Python does not store a string placed after an assignment, so reading the file is the reliable method.
sections.watch_out: The paragraph is found by its opening words, so changing that opening breaks the lookup.

sections.name: TestTheCountsAreDerivedNotStated
sections.title: Forbids written counts and checks the open list
sections.what: Blocks the commentary from stating tallies in prose, because a written count goes stale. It also checks the list of open debts in the commentary names exactly the deferred ids.
sections.why: The docstrings say a written tally was once two short of the table, so the numbers are now derived from the table.
sections.watch_out: The word ban is a plain text match, so a correct sentence that contains a banned phrase will fail.

sections.name: TestEachEntryIsUsable
sections.title: Checks each entry has a date, detail and a deferral reason
sections.what: Checks every entry has a date no later than 1 January 2027 and more than 200 characters of text. It also checks every deferred entry says it is deferred and gives a reason using words such as because, blocked on or not yet.
sections.why: The docstrings state that a deferral with no date or reason looks the same as something forgotten.
sections.watch_out: The length and keyword checks are rough, so a short but real entry can fail while a padded entry with the keywords can pass.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded (part 1)
sections.title: Begins checks that recorded fixes are real
sections.what: Opens the group of checks that confirm each claimed fix in both the spec and the code, covering divergences D1 to D5. Examples: the revision pass count per depth tier matches the spec, the feasibility block sits on the record, the assumptions sit on the future state, and every prerequisite kind has a reason.
sections.why: The class docstring says an entry claiming a fix over a section still showing the old text is the register lying, which is what these checks prevent.
sections.watch_out: These checks depend on exact phrases in SPEC.md, so rewording the spec can break a check without any real change.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d6_the_work_unit_vocabulary_exists_and_is_carried
sections.title: Checks the work unit vocabulary is carried
sections.what: Confirms the WorkUnit set includes an UNSPECIFIED value, that the process match and the record both use that type, and that the match keeps the raw label.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The entry for D6 records it as closed, and this check confirms the fields exist.
sections.watch_out: It checks field types only, not whether the values are filled in correctly.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d7_an_unmeasured_agreement_is_absent_not_neutral
sections.title: Checks unmeasured agreement is absent, not neutral
sections.what: Checks that when agreement was not measured, the confidence result has no agreement value and the agreement is not listed as a contributing feature. It also confirms that a neutral stand-in of one half would have cut the score by a quarter, and the current code does not do that. The section also starts the check of the section 6.4 band table.
sections.why: The D7 entry says unmeasured agreement is excluded rather than set to a neutral value, so this check tests the arithmetic rather than the wording.
sections.watch_out: The expected figures come from the example evidence fixtures, so changing those fixtures moves the expected score.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded (part 4)
sections.title: Checks the band table against recomputed values
sections.what: Recomputes, for each saved candidate record, the confidence now and before, the widening factor now and before, and the band change, then compares each to the matching row of the section 6.4 table. The prior value is taken as the current value times three quarters, following how the entry describes the old formula.
sections.why: The docstring explains that a confidence formula change moves the band a client reads, so the table must not attribute a narrowing to the wrong case.
sections.watch_out: With no saved records on disk, this check fails and asks for a pipeline replay first.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded (part 5)
sections.title: Checks the band figures appear in the prose too
sections.what: Checks the prose introducing the band table, and the D7 entry, both carry each case's band change percentage. It also checks there are exactly two zero-confidence cases, and both places say they are not comparable.
sections.why: The comments say an earlier version fixed the table but left the prose with superseded numbers, so the prose is checked as well.
sections.watch_out: Prose is checked as plain text, so a rounded or reworded figure fails even if it is correct, and the count of two is fixed in the check.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d7_discloses_that_no_migration_is_provided
sections.title: Checks the no-migration disclosure is true
sections.what: Checks that D7 says no migration is provided, and that the claims behind that are true in the repository: evals/results is git-ignored, no tracked fixture carries a confidence block, and the baseline file holds no confidence data. The docstring lists a fourth claim about the checkpoint store, which this code does not check directly.
sections.why: The docstring says the disclosure once went missing from the entry while the summary said it was there, so the disclosure itself is now checked.
sections.watch_out: The git checks need git installed and the code to be a git checkout, otherwise they fail.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d7_records_the_second_fingerprint_move
sections.title: Checks fingerprints, agreement status and a stale claim
sections.what: Checks that D7 records the version moved twice and names the live fingerprint. It checks D14 says the agreement measure is not implemented and gives the model call as the reason, that section 5.4 says the same, that no caller supplies agreement, and that D4 no longer claims nothing was removed.
sections.why: The docstrings say a deferral is only useful if it says what closing it would take, and an entry claiming a state must match the code.
sections.watch_out: The check that no caller supplies agreement is a text search of the source, so a refactor can make it pass or fail wrongly.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d8_the_version_moved_and_the_shape_is_pinned_to_it
sections.title: Checks the schema version and its fingerprint match
sections.what: Checks the set of readable schema versions holds only the current version, the major version number is at least 2, the current shape matches the pinned fingerprint, and the D8 entry names no specific version but states it always equals the schema version.
sections.why: The docstring explains that pinning a literal version failed on a correct version bump, so the check reads the module rather than a fixed number.
sections.watch_out: Any change in the shape of the contract requires the fingerprint, the version and the D8 entry to be updated together, or this fails.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d8_the_failure_at_least_names_the_version
sections.title: Checks version errors, capacity values and a D12 link
sections.what: Checks that loading an old checkpoint file raises a StaleCheckpoint error that includes the version found. It also checks the capacity check accepts only the two values the D11 entry describes, and that the D12 entry names the run cost gap it stacks on.
sections.why: The docstring explains the error test replaced a text search, because a text search would pass on a comment left behind after the raise was removed.
sections.watch_out: The error test writes to a temporary folder, so a change to the stored file format can break it.

sections.name: TestTheAmendmentsActuallyLanded: test_d12_prices_what_it_used_to_only_order
sections.title: Checks priced prerequisites, the open debt and the gap effect
sections.what: Checks declared prerequisites are priced: the pipeline function exists and at least one kind has a build cost above zero. It also checks the cost basis is kept off the run manifest and the D13 entry explains the dependency direction, that the D11 by-function gap stays open because no record has a function field, and that a gap in the confidence measure lowers the score.
sections.why: The docstrings state these as the reasons for the entries; the pricing check guards against a cost that is nominally present but always zero.
sections.watch_out: The pricing check confirms only that some kind has a cost above zero, not that any figure is right.

summary: Checks that the divergence register in SPEC.md stays accurate: each known difference is recorded, each claimed fix is real in both the spec text and the code, and each open item has a stated reason.
purpose: Keeps the list of known differences between the written specification and the built software honest. It fails when a new difference is added without someone acknowledging it here, when an entry claims a fix that the spec or code does not show, or when an open item gives no reason.
why: The docstring states that an unrecorded difference makes the whole spec untrustworthy. Several checks exist because earlier versions of the register described the code wrongly, and the file keeps those lessons.
how: 1) Reads the register part of SPEC.md. 2) Pulls out each entry by its id, status and date. 3) Compares those entries with the REGISTERED table in this file. 4) Checks every entry has a date and enough text, and every deferred entry gives a reason. 5) For each claimed fix, checks the matching spec section text and the code it names, such as field lists, function signatures and enumerated values. 6) Recomputes the section 6.4 band table from saved records and compares it with the spec, row by row. 7) Runs git commands to check ignored files and tracked fixtures.
inputs: SPEC.md, this file's own tables and text, source files under packages, the saved records in evals/results/candidates, the baseline file in evals/results, and the git repository.
outputs: Pass or fail for each check. A failure message names the entry id, the section, or the case that disagrees.
risks: Several checks need files that git does not track, such as evals/results, so they fail on a fresh clone until a replay has been run. Checks match exact wording in SPEC.md, so a rewording can break them without any real change. Some checks use git commands and fail if git is not available.
debug: Read the assertion message first. For an unknown entry id, decide whether the spec should be amended or the id should be added to REGISTERED, as the docstring instructs; do not widen the check. For a band table failure, rerun the replay to regenerate records under evals/results/candidates. For a git failure, confirm git is installed and the tests run inside the repository.
